thread.title: Toyota Re‑enters Philippine Market in Late 1980s with the E90 Corolla
thread.title_full: Toyota Re‑enters Philippine Market in Late 1980s with the E90 Corolla

author: TopGearPh
title: Toyota Re‑enters Philippine Market in Late 1980s with the E90 Corolla
text: Toyota Re‑enters Philippine Market in Late 1980s with the E90 Corolla After the 1986 economic revival, Toyota Motor Corporation re‑entered the Philippines in 1988 with Toyota Motor Philippines. The E90 Corolla, a compact yet feature‑rich model, was introduced to the local market and helped cement Toyota's reputation for quality and innovation. In the late 1980s the Philippine economy was on an upward trajectory after the 1986 EDSA Revolution. By 1986 the country's gross domestic product had recovered from years of decline and inflation had slashed from a peak of more than fifty percent in 1984 to barely a percent. The stock market was also booming, and the Philippine Stock Exchange briefly ranked among the best‑performing exchanges worldwide. It was against this backdrop of economic optimism that Toyota Motor Corporation decided it was the moment to bring its vehicles back to the archipelago.Toyota Motor Philippines Launch DetailsToyota Motor Philippines was formally launched in August 1988 as a joint venture between the Japanese automaker, Dr. George S. K. Ty's Metrobank and Mitsui & Co. The company began retail sales in early 1989 with a slim lineup of three models: the M30 Lite Ace, the S130 Crown and the E90 Corolla. The first Corolla sold a month after launch was a red 1.6‑liter GL model that rolled out of the Bicutan plant on March 3, 1989.By September that year the factory had shifted from semi‑knocked‑down (SKD) to completely‑knocked‑down (CKD) production, signifying a ramp‑up in local manufacturing capacity. The E90, Toyota's sixth‑generation Corolla, was introduced globally in 1987 and was the first to offer front‑wheel‑drive as well as an all‑wheel‑drive configuration. Described by designer Seiiji Fukushima as a clean, aerodynamic shell, it was considerably smaller than its contemporaries, measuring just under 4.2 metres long - a size comparable to today's Yaris Cross.Corolla Engine Specifications And InteriorIn the Philippine market it was offered with either a 1.3‑litre or a 1.6‑litre petrol engine, paired with a four‑ or five‑speed manual gearbox. The 1.3‑litre 2E engine delivered 74 horsepower and, for the 1.6‑litre 4A‑F twin‑cam engine, 94 horsepower - a remarkable figure for a family sedan of that era. Inside, the Corolla replaced the clunky dashboards of previous generations with a more integrated, wrap‑around design.Controls such as the radio, HVAC and gear lever melded into a cohesive cockpit, while the instrument cluster was pared down to essential gauges. The 1.3‑liter models included a speedometer, fuel gauge and water‑temperature readout, whereas the 1.6‑GL added a tachometer. Although the cabin was light and airy for a small sedan, rear seating was best suited for short trips as taller occupants would feel cramped.From an engineering standpoint the Corolla achieved its spaciousness and ease of handling through a fully independent suspension system. MacPherson struts at the front handled the load while coil springs provided a smooth ride. A lower control arm kept the front wheels in place and a stabilizer bar reduced body roll.Suspension And Steering Engineering FeaturesAt the rear a multi‑link strut arrangement with dual lateral links and a trailing arm offered predictable handling; the 1.6‑GL models also featured a factory stabilizer bar to sharpen cornering. Rack‑and‑pinion steering across all variants gave the car a tight 4.9‑metre turning circle, making it well‑suited for urban manoeuvring. The early years of Toyota Motor Philippines set the foundation for a stable and expandable presence in the country.Brand‑new vehicles, improved ergonomics and advanced four‑valve engines created a strong first impression that would help Toyota grow its fleet over the next decades.
summary: The E90 Corolla, a compact yet feature‑rich model, was introduced to the local market and helped cement Toyota's reputation for quality and innovation. The first Corolla sold a month after launch was a red 1.6‑liter GL model that rolled out of the Bicutan plant on March 3, 1989.By September that year the factory had shifted from semi‑knocked‑down (SKD) to completely‑knocked‑down (CKD) production, signifying a ramp‑up in local manufacturing capacity.
